question.text: Two capacitors, each having capacitance <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>40</mn><mi>μ</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">F</mi></math> are connected in series. The space between one of the capacitors is filled with dielectric material of dielectric constant <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>K</mi></math> such that the equivalence capacitance of the system became <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>24</mn><mi>μ</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">F</mi></math>. The value of <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>K</mi></math> will be :

solution.text:
When a dielectric is inserted between the sheets of a capacitor, its capacitance becomes KC.

Now the equivalent capacitance in series combination will be,

Ceq=C×KCC1+K⇒24=40K1+K⇒K=1.5
